why: The statement asks whether N(t) is uniformly bounded for all t >= 2. King and Williams (online 31 August 2026, after the snapshot) prove boundedness for a restricted class of t (those with proportionately large prime-power factors): a restriction of the question, so case; it was accepted by a refereed journal of record (NNTDM), which meets the digestion bar, and nothing in the record gives a specific reason to doubt it. MRSTT 2021 settles the interior region for large t: case, refereed in QJM, before the snapshot. Kane and Abbott-Erdős-Hanson give growing bounds on N(t), so bound. Singmaster's 1975 census and de Weger's six-fold value are finite instances; the six-fold family is compatible with boundedness and neither witnesses nor contradicts the statement. Jenkins (a different equation), de Koninck et al. (multinomial), Bazsó et al. (Stirling numbers) and the gcd criterion (gcds, not multiplicities) are variants. The gcd paper credits an AI agent, but the record leaves its systems list empty and the result is not about this problem, so its AI role is none. No AI role was found in any event that bears on the problem.
doubts: King and Williams: the full text was not read, so the exact class of t and the corollary N(t) <= 2r rest on the abstract and a search snippet. The paper has had no outside engagement in six weeks, and I count it as digested only because a refereed journal accepted it. The record left open whether Erdős 849 is among the AlphaProof Nexus resolutions, but that database states a different (existence) form of the problem.
